name: Dermata Therapeutics, Inc.

profile.description: Dermata Therapeutics is a San Diego micro-cap that in September 2025 pivoted from prescription dermatology drug development (its Spongilla-based XYNGARI acne candidate) to over-the-counter, direct-to-consumer skincare, withdrawing the XYNGARI IND [3][1]. Its Tome Skincare brand (a once-weekly foundational treatment and a clearing treatment for acne) was scheduled to launch commercially on August 25, 2026 [1]. The company had $4.4M of cash at June 30, 2026, guided to fund operations only into Q4 2026, has 9 employees and a market cap of roughly $3.8M [2][6]. The CEO is Gerald (Gerry) Proehl [6].

innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The 2025 pivot from Rx drug development to the Tome DTC skincare brand is a real business-model change, but the first product only reached market in late August 2026 and no sales have been reported, so it has not yet opened a proven revenue stream [1][3]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI strategy, product or internal savings were found in company materials [1][4]. Market Share (0/2): Pre-revenue entrant in a crowded OTC acne/skincare market with no share data. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management says additional product launches will follow Tome Foundational Treatment, but no dates or revenue visibility are given [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D fell to $0.21M in Q2 2026 after XYNGARI was shelved, now below biotech peers [6].
innovation.label: WEAK

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Management framed the OTC pivot around improving patient access and affordability of acne treatment — a clear purpose consistent with the Inspire 'Product Access and Affordability' attribution, but not distinctive or validated by execution [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable or community programs found. Employee Retention (0/2): A 9-person company with no retention disclosures. Insider Buying (0/2): Officers and directors (including the CEO and CFO) participated in a January 2025 PIPE, but that is outside the last 12 months and no 2026 insider purchases were found [5].
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a growth stock on the few metrics available: 2.5/10, rounded to 3. Liquidity passes on Yahoo's three-month average of ~3.39M shares × $0.77 = ~$2.6M/day, but this is skewed by spike days — FMP's average is ~530K shares (~$0.41M/day) and recent sessions trade under 120K shares, so the stock is functionally near IOWN's $1M floor [6]. D/E of 0% scores 1.0 (no debt on the June 30, 2026 balance sheet). ROE of -184% scores 0 at 2x weight and forward P/E of -0.20 scores 0 (negative). Revenue growth, 5-year revenue CAGR, profit margin and PEG are excluded because the company has reported no product revenue and has negative earnings [6].
infrastructure.label: WEAK

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): PROTECTED. Dermata sells physical topical skincare products; AI cannot substitute for the product itself, and no analyst has flagged AI substitution risk [1]. The score stops short of IMMUNE because the DTC model competes for attention on digital channels where AI-optimized marketing by much larger brands raises customer-acquisition costs. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue.
ai_resilience.label: MODERATE

infinite_game.summary: Dermata is in survival mode rather than playing an infinite game. The company abandoned its lead prescription asset and a decade of clinical work to chase faster DTC revenue because cash was running out, has executed multiple reverse splits to keep its Nasdaq listing, and now has a runway only into Q4 2026 [2][5]. Sinek would see a finite player whose strategy is dictated by the next financing.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Accessible, affordable acne treatment' is a reasonable purpose, but it was articulated as the rationale for a cash-driven pivot and is interchangeable with many skincare brands; it has not shaped decisions over time [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): With 9 employees, repeated restructuring from clinical to commercial operations, and a runway measured in months, there is no evidence of an organization with the stability Sinek's circle of safety requires [2][6].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary acknowledging competitors' strengths or learning from established OTC acne brands was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Withdrawing the XYNGARI IND and relaunching as a DTC consumer brand is a dramatic shift, but it was driven by financing pressure rather than a Just Cause, so it earns partial credit [1][3].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Decisions have been reactive — reverse splits in 2023, 2024 and 2025 to cure Nasdaq bid-price deficiencies, ATM sales (~$1.9M in H1 2026) and the pivot itself — rather than costly long-term bets [2][5].

investment_thesis: The bull case is optionality on a tiny base: Dermata carries no debt, launched its first commercial product (Tome Foundational Treatment) in August 2026, and at a ~$3.8M market cap even modest DTC traction would be material [1][6]. The OTC route removes FDA approval risk and costly Phase 3 trials, letting the company generate revenue far sooner than its prior XYNGARI path [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case dominates. Cash was $4.4M at June 30, 2026 after $4.9M of H1 operating cash burn, and management guided that it would fund operations only into Q4 2026 — i.e., now — so further dilutive financing or a going-concern event is likely [1][2]. ROE is -184%, there is no reported revenue yet, the company has used three reverse splits to stay listed, and the stock trades at $0.77, below Nasdaq's $1 minimum bid again [5][6].
key_catalysts: First reported Tome Skincare sales in the Q3 2026 report, establishing whether DTC customer acquisition is economic [1]
Additional Tome product launches planned after the foundational treatment, broadening the DTC basket [4]
Any non-dilutive partnership or retail distribution deal that extends the runway beyond Q4 2026 [2]
key_risks: Cash runway only into Q4 2026 ($4.4M cash at June 30, 2026) makes another highly dilutive raise or going-concern doubt near-certain [1][2]
Nasdaq listing risk: shares at ~$0.77 are below the $1 minimum bid, and a prior delisting determination in 2025 followed repeated reverse splits [5][6]
DTC skincare is crowded and marketing-intensive; a 9-person company with no brand history may be unable to acquire customers profitably [2]
